get.description:
Query all available jobs.

GET /jobs
Retrieves a list of job execution records with optional filtering, pagination, and sorting.

This endpoint returns job execution data based on various query parameters such as job ID, user, job name, state, and time-based filters. The response includes full job records by default.

Query Parameters:
complete_data (bool, deprecated):
Deprecated. Previously used to toggle between full and partial job records. Now always returns full job records.

job_id (str, optional):
Filter results by a specific job ID.

job_attempt_index (str, optional):
Filter by job attempt index. Note: Cannot be used on its own—must be combined with job_id.

user (str, optional):
Filter results by the username who submitted the job.

job_name (str, optional):
Filter results by the job name.

workflow_id (str, optional):
Filter results by the exact canonical workflow ID.

job_name_match (str, optional):
How to match job_name: "prefix" (default, starts with) or "exact".

state (str, optional):
Filter by job state (e.g., Slurm job states).
Cannot be used together with completed_jobs.

completed_jobs (bool, optional):
Filter by job completion status.
If True, returns completed jobs; if False, returns running jobs.
Cannot be used with state.

reconciliation_eligible_jobs (bool, default=False):
Return the state-based candidate set used to seed scheduler reconciliation:
every non-final job plus failure-like terminal jobs. COMPLETED and REQUEUED
are excluded because their recovery is driven by exact-attempt Advice.
Cannot be used with state or completed_jobs.

offset (int, default=0):
Number of records to skip (used for pagination).

time_filter_target (JobTimeFilterTarget, optional):
Specifies which job time field (created, started, etc.) to filter by.
Requires either time_filter_from or time_filter_to.

time_filter_from (datetime, optional):
Start of time range for the selected time filter target.

time_filter_to (datetime, optional):
End of time range for the selected time filter target.

sort_by (str, optional):
Comma-separated list of fields to sort by. Each field can specify order as asc or desc.
Example: job_id:asc,job_attempt_index:desc

job_group_id (str, optional):
Filter by job group ID. Returns all job attempts belonging to this job group.

include_job_group_attempts (bool, default=True):
When job_group_id is not provided, controls whether to include job attempts that belong to a job group.
When False, only returns standalone job attempts (not part of any job group).
Ignored when job_group_id is provided.

Returns:
A JobExecutionStatuses object containing the list of job execution records that match the filter criteria.

get.description:
Analyze node sets across multiple jobs using set algebra expressions.

This endpoint evaluates set algebra expressions over job node lists to identify
commonalities and differences between jobs. It supports union (U), intersection (&),
and difference (-) operations.

Query Parameters:
    expr (str, required):
        Set algebra expression using job IDs in format 'job_id/attempt_index'.
        Supported operators:
        - U: Union (nodes in either set)
        - &: Intersection (nodes in both sets)
        - -: Difference (nodes in first set but not second)
        - ( ): Parentheses for grouping
        Examples:
        - "12345/0 U 12346/0" (union of two jobs)
        - "(12345/0 U 12346/0) - 12347/0" (union then subtract)
        - "12345/0 & 12346/0 & 12347/0" (common nodes across three jobs)

    group_by (str, optional):
        How to group the result nodes. Options: "rack" or "none".
        Default is "none". When set to "rack", nodes are grouped by their
        rack identifier (only applicable for clusters with rack-based node naming).

Returns:
    NodeAnalysisResponse:
        Contains the computed node set, optionally grouped by rack, along with
        metadata about the expression and jobs queried.

Raises:
    400 Bad Request:
        - Invalid expression syntax
        - Invalid group_by value
        - Expression references too many jobs (max 100)
    404 Not Found:
        - One or more job IDs not found in database
    500 Internal Server Error:
        - Database errors
        - Unexpected failures

schema.description: Set algebra expression (e.g., '12345/0 U 12346/0 - 12347/0')

This model matches the NVIDIA Recovery Go client schema (flattened structure) rather than

AnomalyDetectionConfig.title: AnomalyDetectionConfig
AnomalyDetectionConfig.description:
Anomaly detection configuration that the user can control per job.

Attributes:
    log_based_crash_enabled (bool): Whether to enable log-based crash detection for the job.
        If set to False, a CRASH anomaly will be generated immediately when the job enters FAILED
        state, without waiting for log analysis. Default is True (log-based detection enabled).
    log_based_timeout_enabled (bool): Whether to enable log-based no-output timeout detection
        (HANGNOOUTPUT) for the job. When set to False, the watcher service will suppress
        HANGNOOUTPUT anomaly publication for the job. Default is True (detection enabled).
    log_based_timeout_threshold_pretraining (int): Per-job no-output timeout threshold (in
        seconds) applied during the pre-training phase. The watcher uses this value as the
        silence window after which a HANGNOOUTPUT anomaly may be raised. Must be a positive
        integer. Default is 960 seconds (16 minutes).
    log_based_timeout_threshold_trainingloop (int): Per-job no-output timeout threshold (in
        seconds) applied during the training loop phase. The watcher uses this value as the
        silence window after which a HANGNOOUTPUT anomaly may be raised. Must be a positive
        integer. Default is 840 seconds (14 minutes).

ApsSlurmJobSpec-Input.title: ApsSlurmJobSpec
ApsSlurmJobSpec-Input.description:
APS Slurm Job Spec, today this spec should be passed to APS as a JSON string included in the "comment" of a Slurm
job.

Attributes:
    workflow_id (Optional[str]): The workflow this Slurm job belongs to.
    workflow_name (Optional[str]): Deprecated alias for workflow_id.
    environment (Optional[str]): The APS/NVIDIA Recovery environment that the job should be managed by, if not specified,
        the job will be managed by the "prod" environment.
    auto_resume_mode (Optional[AutoResumeModeEnum]): The auto resume mode for the job.
    max_requeue_times (Optional[PositiveInt]): The max number of requeue that will happen to the job. Only
        applicable when auto_resume_mode is set to REQUEUE. If not specified, the system wide max job attempt limit
        will be used. Note that the max requeue times will be capped at the system wide limit too.
    requeue_on_completion (Optional[bool]): Whether to requeue the job on normal completion. Default is None which
        means it follows the system wide default. Setting it to either True or False will override the system wide
        default. Only meaningful when auto_resume_mode is set to REQUEUE.
    log_file_paths_shared_across_attempts (bool): Whether requeued attempts intentionally write to the same log
        files. Defaults to False, which requires unique per-attempt paths and protects event correlation from
        stale paths returned by Slurm during a requeue race.
    nvrx (Optional[bool]): Whether the job is enabled for NVRX. Default is "disabled".
    anomaly_detection_config (AnomalyDetectionConfig): Anomaly detection configuration. Defaults to
        AnomalyDetectionConfig() (all log-based detections enabled with default thresholds). Use
        AnomalyDetectionConfig(log_based_crash_enabled=False) to generate a CRASH anomaly immediately when the
        job enters FAILED state. Use AnomalyDetectionConfig(log_based_timeout_enabled=False) to suppress
        log-based no-output (HANGNOOUTPUT) anomalies, or override
        log_based_timeout_threshold_pretraining / log_based_timeout_threshold_trainingloop to tune the
        per-phase silence window before a HANGNOOUTPUT anomaly may fire.
    dag_dependencies (Optional[list[DagDependencyStep]]): DAG dependencies that must be satisfied before this
        job can run. Each step specifies a dependency job and a trigger condition. The current job will only be
        eligible for execution when all dependencies are met.
    dag_action (Optional[DagActionEnum]): The action to take on this job after all its dag_dependencies are
        satisfied. For example, RELEASE will release the job so it becomes eligible for scheduling.

ApsSlurmJobSpec-Output.title: ApsSlurmJobSpec
ApsSlurmJobSpec-Output.description:
APS Slurm Job Spec, today this spec should be passed to APS as a JSON string included in the "comment" of a Slurm
job.

Attributes:
    workflow_id (Optional[str]): The workflow this Slurm job belongs to.
    workflow_name (Optional[str]): Deprecated alias for workflow_id.
    environment (Optional[str]): The APS/NVIDIA Recovery environment that the job should be managed by, if not specified,
        the job will be managed by the "prod" environment.
    auto_resume_mode (Optional[AutoResumeModeEnum]): The auto resume mode for the job.
    max_requeue_times (Optional[PositiveInt]): The max number of requeue that will happen to the job. Only
        applicable when auto_resume_mode is set to REQUEUE. If not specified, the system wide max job attempt limit
        will be used. Note that the max requeue times will be capped at the system wide limit too.
    requeue_on_completion (Optional[bool]): Whether to requeue the job on normal completion. Default is None which
        means it follows the system wide default. Setting it to either True or False will override the system wide
        default. Only meaningful when auto_resume_mode is set to REQUEUE.
    log_file_paths_shared_across_attempts (bool): Whether requeued attempts intentionally write to the same log
        files. Defaults to False, which requires unique per-attempt paths and protects event correlation from
        stale paths returned by Slurm during a requeue race.
    nvrx (Optional[bool]): Whether the job is enabled for NVRX. Default is "disabled".
    anomaly_detection_config (AnomalyDetectionConfig): Anomaly detection configuration. Defaults to
        AnomalyDetectionConfig() (all log-based detections enabled with default thresholds). Use
        AnomalyDetectionConfig(log_based_crash_enabled=False) to generate a CRASH anomaly immediately when the
        job enters FAILED state. Use AnomalyDetectionConfig(log_based_timeout_enabled=False) to suppress
        log-based no-output (HANGNOOUTPUT) anomalies, or override
        log_based_timeout_threshold_pretraining / log_based_timeout_threshold_trainingloop to tune the
        per-phase silence window before a HANGNOOUTPUT anomaly may fire.
    dag_dependencies (Optional[list[DagDependencyStep]]): DAG dependencies that must be satisfied before this
        job can run. Each step specifies a dependency job and a trigger condition. The current job will only be
        eligible for execution when all dependencies are met.
    dag_action (Optional[DagActionEnum]): The action to take on this job after all its dag_dependencies are
        satisfied. For example, RELEASE will release the job so it becomes eligible for scheduling.

AutoResumeModeEnum.title: AutoResumeModeEnum
AutoResumeModeEnum.description:
This enum class defines the auto resume mode for the job.

SINGLETON_DEPENDENCY: NVIDIA Recovery will use the existing singleton dependency jobs to resume the progress.
REQUEUE: NVIDIA Recovery will requeue the same job to resume the progress.

DagActionEnum.title: DagActionEnum
DagActionEnum.description:
The action to take on the target job in a DAG step.

RELEASE: Release the target job so it becomes eligible for scheduling.

DagDependencyReasonCodeEnum.title: DagDependencyReasonCodeEnum
DagDependencyReasonCodeEnum.description: Machine-readable explanation for the latest DAG dependency evaluation.

action_status.title: Action Status
action_status.description: Dependency action status: not_eligible, in_progress, successful, failed, or aborted. Aborted is absorbing and means a parent reached terminal Advice, so this gate cannot release.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable explanation for the latest dependency evaluation.

reason_message.title: Reason Message
reason_message.description: Human-readable explanation for the latest dependency evaluation; clients must not parse it.

reason_details.title: Reason Details
reason_details.description: Structured context for the latest dependency evaluation.

last_evaluated_at.title: Last Evaluated At
last_evaluated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the latest dependency evaluation; null before the first evaluation.

DagDependencyResponse.title: DagDependencyResponse
DagDependencyResponse.description:
Public-facing data model for a DAG dependency record.

Each record represents a dependency relationship between a dependent (child) job and a dependency (parent) job.
When the parent job satisfies the trigger condition, the dependent job becomes eligible for the specified action.

DagDependencyStep.title: DagDependencyStep
DagDependencyStep.description:
A single DAG dependency step that describes a dependency that must meet a trigger condition
before the current job can run.

Attributes:
    target (JobReference): The dependency job, identified by name or id.
    trigger (DagTriggerConditionEnum): The condition that triggers this step. Defaults to COMPLETED.

DagTriggerConditionEnum.title: DagTriggerConditionEnum
DagTriggerConditionEnum.description:
The condition under which a DAG step should be triggered.

COMPLETED: Trigger when the current job finishes successfully (Slurm COMPLETED state).

GetRecoverySequenceResponse.title: GetRecoverySequenceResponse
GetRecoverySequenceResponse.description: Canonical context of an existing backend-owned recovery sequence.

GetWorkflowsResponse.title: GetWorkflowsResponse
GetWorkflowsResponse.description:
The public facing data model of the jobs by name response that gets
returned from job manager's REST APIs. It contains a list of JobsByName
objects.

GlobalEvent.title: GlobalEvent
GlobalEvent.description:
Represents a global (job-level) event that occurred during job execution.

Unlike NodeEvent, GlobalEvent represents issues that affect the entire job
rather than being attributable to specific nodes. These events don't have
node-specific fields like node name, exclusion_type, job_start_time, job_end_time, or cluster.

Attributes:
    job_id: ID of the job associated with this event
    job_attempt_index: Index of the job attempt
    timestamp: When the event occurred
    job_execution_error: The associated error details
    error_attribution: Classification of the error
    error_attribution_type: Type of telemetry data used for attribution
    error_attribution_origin: Origin of the attribution
    error_attribution_sources: Sources of the attribution
    fact_status: Status of the FACT service

Issue-Input.title: Issue
Issue-Input.description:
Describes a detected issue for a job.

This model is compatible with the NVIDIA Recovery Advice CRD and matches the Go client schema.
Issue types include: CRASH, HANG, STRAGGLER, etc.

Issue-Output.title: Issue
Issue-Output.description:
Describes a detected issue for a job.

This model is compatible with the NVIDIA Recovery Advice CRD and matches the Go client schema.
Issue types include: CRASH, HANG, STRAGGLER, etc.

JobAnomaly.title: JobAnomaly
JobAnomaly.description:
Class to represent an anomaly that happened during the job execution.

Note: Today given this model is very simple, it's also directly returned
from job manager's REST API. We can introduce a new model and migrate the
internal data model to it when we need to distinguish them.

Note that for newly created JobAnomaly the default value for `processed` is False,
but old data read from the storage, the default value will be set to None to provide
correct semantic because they will never be set to True or False.

JobCheckpointInfo.title: JobCheckpointInfo
JobCheckpointInfo.description: Data structure that represents a job checkpoint event.

JobExecutionError.title: JobExecutionError
JobExecutionError.description:
Represents an error that occurred during job execution.

This model captures details about errors including their type, code, signature,
and descriptive information to help with debugging and error tracking.

Attributes:
    code: The error code if available, zero otherwise
    message: Short error message
    description: Detailed description of the error
    signature: A unique signature identifying this specific error

JobExecutionStatuses.title: JobExecutionStatuses
JobExecutionStatuses.description:
This class is used to return a list of job execution statuses from the job manager's REST API. Since the response is
paginated, this class also contains the total number of items that match the query.

JobGroupStatus.title: JobGroupStatus
JobGroupStatus.description:
The public facing data model of a job group's aggregated metadata, derived from
the job execution records belonging to the group.

JobGroupStatuses.title: JobGroupStatuses
JobGroupStatuses.description:
This class is used to return a list of job group statuses from the job manager's REST API. Since the response is
paginated, this class also contains the total number of items that match the query.

JobReferenceById.title: JobReferenceById
JobReferenceById.description: Identify a target job by its Slurm job ID.

JobReferenceByName.title: JobReferenceByName
JobReferenceByName.description: Identify a target job by its name.

JobTimeFilterTarget.title: JobTimeFilterTarget
JobTimeFilterTarget.description:
The target job time to use in a time filter query. Jobs have different times, such
as the submit, start, end times and the last updated time. This enum
allows selecting one of these for time filter queries when retrieving jobs by time.

ListAdviceResponse.title: ListAdviceResponse
ListAdviceResponse.description: Response model for listing advice records.

ListDagDependenciesResponse.title: ListDagDependenciesResponse
ListDagDependenciesResponse.description:
Response model for listing DAG dependency records. The response is paginated —
item_count reflects the total number of matching records, not the page size.

expression.title: Expression
expression.description: The original expression that was evaluated

groupedByRack.title: Groupedbyrack
groupedByRack.description: Nodes grouped by rack identifier (only present when group_by=rack)

jobsQueried.title: Jobsqueried
jobsQueried.description: List of job IDs (format: job_id/attempt_index) that were queried

NodeAnalysisResponse.title: NodeAnalysisResponse
NodeAnalysisResponse.description:
Response model for node set analysis endpoint.

This response contains the result of evaluating a set algebra expression
over job node lists, optionally grouped by rack.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: List of node names in the result set

count.title: Count
count.description: Total number of nodes in the result set

NodeAnalysisResult.title: NodeAnalysisResult
NodeAnalysisResult.description: Result of node set analysis containing the computed node set.

NodeConstraints.title: NodeConstraints
NodeConstraints.description:
Contains scheduling constraints for a job.

This model is compatible with the NVIDIA Recovery Advice CRD and matches the Go client schema.

NodeEvent.title: NodeEvent
NodeEvent.description:
Represents an event that occurred on a node during job execution.

This model captures details about node events including error attribution,
timestamps, and relationships to jobs and errors.

Attributes:
    job_id: ID of the job associated with this event
    job_attempt_index: Index of the job attempt
    node: Name of the node where the event occurred
    timestamp: When the event occurred
    attribution: Classification of the error (hardware/software/system/unknown)
    attribution_type: Type of telemetry data used for attribution
    attribution_origin: Origin of the attribution
    attribution_sources: Sources of the attribution
    actions: Actions taken by ADI
    fact_status: Status of the FACT service
    error: The associated error details

NodeEvents.title: NodeEvents
NodeEvents.description:
Represents a collection of node events and global events.

This model contains lists of NodeEvent and GlobalEvent objects and provides metadata
about the total number of items and the page size.

TODO: Rename this class to something more generic like `AttributionEvents` or
`ErrorAttributions` since it now contains both node-level and global/job-level events,
not just node events.

RemediationAction.title: RemediationAction
RemediationAction.description:
Describes a specific action to take to remediate an issue.

This model is compatible with the NVIDIA Recovery Advice CRD and matches the Go client schema.

ResourceDetail.title: ResourceDetail
ResourceDetail.description:
Represents details about a specific resource involved in a remediation action.

This model is compatible with the NVIDIA Recovery Advice CRD and matches the Go client schema.

SlurmJobExecutionStatus-Input.title: SlurmJobExecutionStatus
SlurmJobExecutionStatus-Input.description:
The public facing data model of the Slurm job execution status that gets
returned from job manager's REST APIs. It contains a subset fields of the
internal data model (SlurmJobExecutionRecord class) to achieve separation.

SlurmJobExecutionStatus-Output.title: SlurmJobExecutionStatus
SlurmJobExecutionStatus-Output.description:
The public facing data model of the Slurm job execution status that gets
returned from job manager's REST APIs. It contains a subset fields of the
internal data model (SlurmJobExecutionRecord class) to achieve separation.

SystemRequeueConfig.title: SystemRequeueConfig
SystemRequeueConfig.description:
Configuration class for system requeue behavior settings.

Attributes:
- max_requeue_times: Controls the maximum number of requeue that the system allows a job to have. Together
    with the job level requeue limit, the lower value will be used to determine the actual requeue limit. In the
    rare case of it set to None, it means the system allows unlimited requeue. "-1" is a special value that means
    infinitely requeue.

- checkpoint_based_requeue_stop_threshold: Controls after how many job attempts without a successful checkpoint,
    the system will stop requeueing the job. This is a system wide setting and will be applied to all jobs. If not
    configured, the system will not use checkpoint signal to stop the requeue sequence.

- requeue_on_completion: Controls whether the system should continue requeuing a job when it's final state is
  COMPLETED.

Workflow.title: Workflow
Workflow.description:
A workflow is a collection of jobs for a particular workload or logical job.

For example, a job maybe requeued multiple times, resulting in a workflow.
